newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon charges seven men for dealing with Israel.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon charges seven men for dealing with Israel.

text.p: A Beirut military investigative judge on Friday charged seven Lebanese men with collaborating with Israel, an offence carrying up to 10 years in jail, judicial sources said.
Judge Riyad Talee' charged the alleged agents with "contacting the Israeli enemy and its agents, giving the enemy information and plotting against Lebanon".
They include two Lebanese soldiers, a former soldier, a general security officer, an editor in a private television station and two other men. All are in custody.
Lebanese citizens are forbidden from dealing with Israel as Lebanon is officially at war with the Jewish state despite more than five years of on-again, off-again peace talks.
Last month, military judicial authorities charged 91 Lebanese on similar grounds.
Some 1,000 Israeli troops and 3,000 allied Lebanese militiamen occupy a 15-km (nine-mile) wide border zone in south Lebanon.
